title: All levels of a coherent formal module have the same support
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] with quasi-compact underlying space), $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\ge1}$ an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Then $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_n)=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_1)$ for every $n\ge1$, where $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=\{x\in X:\mathcal F_x\ne0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (2).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), first sentence of the proof of (1) ('Then Supp(F_n) = Supp(F_1) for all n >= 1'), stated there without proof

proof.text: Fix $n\ge1$ and $x\in X$, and write $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $\mathfrak a=\mathcal I_x\subseteq A$ (an ideal of $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk] (1)) and $M=(\mathcal F_{n+1})_x$, an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. By the definition of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (1), $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F_{n+1}=0$ and the transition map induces an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$. Taking stalks at $x$ (a functor, so isomorphisms go to isomorphisms) and applying [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk] (4) with $\mathcal J=\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_{n+1}$ gives $\mathfrak a^{n+1}M=(\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F_{n+1})_x=0$ and an isomorphism of $A$-modules $M/\mathfrak a^nM\cong(\mathcal F_n)_x$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), proof of (1), first sentence; stated there without proof

proof.text: Algebra: for an ideal $\mathfrak a$ of a ring $A$ and an $A$-module $M$ with $\mathfrak a^{n+1}M=0$ ($n\ge1$), $M/\mathfrak a^nM=0$ implies $M=0$. Indeed $M=\mathfrak a^nM$ gives $M=\mathfrak a^n(\mathfrak a^nM)=\mathfrak a^{2n}M\subseteq\mathfrak a^{n+1}M=0$, since $2n\ge n+1$. (No finiteness of $M$ and no Nakayama lemma is needed.) Conversely $M=0$ gives $M/\mathfrak a^nM=0$. With step 1: $(\mathcal F_n)_x=0$ if and only if $(\mathcal F_{n+1})_x=0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), proof of (1), first sentence; stated there without proof

proof.text: By the definition of the support [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (2), $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_m)=\{x:(\mathcal F_m)_x\ne0\}$, so step 2, valid for every $x\in X$, says $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_n)=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_{n+1})$ for every $n\ge1$. Induction on $n$ gives $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_n)=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_1)$ for all $n\ge1$. (Neither the Noetherian hypothesis nor the coherence of the $\mathcal F_n$ is used.)
